# Grip Wrench Reduction

## Status

Evidence class: derived, provisional. This chapter records the grip-wrench
reduction delivered by GCV-7 (#11713), and the engine-agnostic extraction
helpers from GCV-8 (#11714) that feed it, so they can be inventoried. It is not
approved. The registry blocker `UP-D1-grip-wrench-reduction-inventory` stays
open until UP-D1 inventories the pathway and a human reviews it.

## Purpose

Reduce the two hand-on-club loads to the quantities shown by every engine and
display surface:

- each hand's wrench at its grip point;
- the net force drawn at the grip midpoint;
- the equivalent couple about that midpoint, split into the moment of the
  hand forces and the hands' free torques;
- each hand's moment of force about the midpoint;
- optionally, the net force and couple in club-local axes.

## Conventions

- Sign (binding, ADR-0052): every wrench is the loading **exerted by the hand on
  the club**.
- World frame, SI units: force in N, position in m, moment in N·m.
- Hand $h \in \{L, R\}$ acts at grip point $r_h$ with force $F_h$ and free
  torque $\tau_h$. A free torque may be unavailable when an engine does not
  supply it; it is then absent, not zero.
- Every result records `split_method`. The left/right split of two rigid welds
  is indeterminate and is set by the solver: `constraint_multiplier`,
  `efc_force`, `allocation`, `logged` or `unavailable`. The compliant `bushing`
  grip makes the split determinate. `contact` is reserved for a distributed
  contact grip and is not produced yet.

## Equations

1. Grip midpoint and net force:
   $$r_M = \tfrac{1}{2}\left(r_L + r_R\right), \qquad R = F_L + F_R$$
2. Moment of force of each hand about the midpoint:
   $$MOF_h = (r_h - r_M) \times F_h$$
3. Equivalent couple at the midpoint:
   $$M_M = \underbrace{MOF_L + MOF_R}_{\text{contact force moment}}
     + \underbrace{\tau_L + \tau_R}_{\text{applied free torque}}$$
4. Club-local values, given an orthonormal world-from-club rotation $Q$:
   $R_{local} = Q^{\top} R$ and $M_{M,local} = Q^{\top} M_M$.
5. Holding-hand wrench (GCV-8). With one closed weld, only the *closing* hand
   has a constraint multiplier. The *holding* hand follows from the club's
   Newton-Euler equations, with club mass $m$, centre of mass $c$, world inertia
   $I$ about $c$, gravity $g$, angular velocity $\omega$ and angular
   acceleration $\alpha$:
   $$F_{hold} = m\,(a_c - g) - F_{close}$$
   $$\tau_{hold} = I\alpha + \omega \times (I\omega) - \tau_{close}
     - (r_{close} - c) \times F_{close} - (r_{hold} - c) \times F_{hold}$$
6. Reference minimum-norm split, used to compare a determinate (`bushing`) grip
   with a rigid weld. Take both free torques as zero and let
   $h = \tfrac{1}{2}(r_R - r_L)$. Solve $F_L + F_R = R$ and
   $h \times (F_R - F_L) = M_M$ with minimum $|F_L|^2 + |F_R|^2$:
   $$F_{L,R} = \tfrac{1}{2}\left(R \mp \frac{M_M \times h}{h \cdot h}\right)$$
   The component of $M_M$ along $h$ cannot be produced by forces and is dropped,
   and the axial force is split equally.

The postconditions $M_M = (MOF_L + MOF_R) + (\tau_L + \tau_R)$ and
contact force moment $= MOF_L + MOF_R$ hold exactly. Wrench transport uses the
shared `force_overlay.conversions.move_wrench_point`; no second transport
routine exists.

## Unavailable Values

- If either hand wrench is missing, the midpoint, net force, couple and moments
  of force are unavailable.
- If either free torque is missing, the applied free torque and the couple are
  unavailable, while the net force and moments of force remain.
- An engine that supplies only one six-component grip wrench (for example the
  Pinocchio allocation) reports the net wrench with no per-hand split.

Unavailable values are `None` in an analysis, NaN in a series and `null` over
the API, each with an `unavailable_reason`. They are never reported as zero.

## Implementation

| Symbol | Location |
| --- | --- |
| `HandWrench`, `analyze_grip`, `GripAnalysis`, `GripSeries` | `src/shared/python/biomechanics/grip_wrench.py` |
| `allocate_min_norm`, `about_axis` | `src/shared/python/biomechanics/grip_wrench.py` |
| `to_overlay_wrenches` (labels `grip:hand_*`, `grip:net_midpoint`, `grip:couple_midpoint`, `grip:mof_*`) | `src/shared/python/biomechanics/grip_wrench.py` |
| `holding_hand_wrench`, `net_only_analysis`, `unavailable_analysis` | `src/shared/python/biomechanics/grip_extraction.py` |

Both modules are pure numpy with no engine imports. The per-engine adapters
supply hand points, multiplier-derived wrenches and club kinematics. They are
outside this chapter.

## Tests and Reproduction

```bash
python3 -m pytest tests/unit/biomechanics/test_grip_wrench.py \
  tests/unit/biomechanics/test_grip_extraction.py -q
```

These tests check the algebra against hand-computed wrenches and the stated
postconditions: couple decomposition, moments of force, club-local rotation,
the Newton-Euler holding-hand recovery and the minimum-norm split. They do not
check any engine's constraint solver or grip model.

## Assumptions and Limitations

- The club is a rigid body. The holding-hand recovery is only as accurate as
  the club mass, inertia and accelerations supplied by the engine.
- For two rigid welds the per-hand split is a solver artefact. Only the net
  force and couple at the midpoint are determinate, so per-hand values must be
  read together with `split_method`.
- These are software outputs of each engine's grip model, not measured hand
  loads. No comparison with instrumented-grip measurements has been made for
  this pathway.
- No uncertainty or tolerance against an external reference has been
  established; none is claimed.
- Reference derivation: `docs/research/proximal_distal_energy_transfer/`,
  section "Reduction of Two Contacts to an Equivalent Wrench".

## Prescribed-Motion Bushing Parity Integration

F10i #12060 integrates `main` at
`26316150998ede86d08b59f1686d8b80ff9f8bdf`, including the separate #11739
prescribed-motion bushing pathway. Its maintained method is
`src/shared/python/grip_contact/bushing_law.py`; prescribed hand motion and
per-engine force adapters are separate from the wrench reduction above.

Let $R_h,R_c$ map hand and club frame components into world coordinates,
$a=p_c-p_h$, and let all positions, velocities and angular velocities below
be world quantities. Define

$$
\delta=R_h^T a,\qquad
\dot\delta=R_h^T(v_c-v_h-\omega_h\times a),\qquad
\theta=\operatorname{BodyXYZ}(R_h^T R_c).
$$

For the body-fixed X-Y-Z sequence, the implemented matrix $N(\theta)$ maps
moving-frame angular velocity into angle rates:

$$
\dot\theta=N(\theta)R_c^T(\omega_c-\omega_h),\qquad
F=-R_h(K_t\delta+C_t\dot\delta),\qquad
M=-R_cN(\theta)^T(K_r\theta+C_r\dot\theta).
$$

Here $F$ and $M$ are the world wrench on the club at its bushing frame.
The transpose follows from virtual power; rotational spring coordinates
cannot be substituted directly for Cartesian moments at finite rotation.
Diagonal stiffness and damping have units N/m, N s/m, N m/rad and
N m s/rad. The source refuses the X-Y-Z singularity margin. The method
requires declared rigid frame attachments, twist conventions and parameters;
it does not calibrate those parameters against measured grip loads.

Run `pytest --noconftest -o addopts='' tests/unit/grip_contact -q` in the
existing native environment. The F10i main-integration run uses OpenSim 4.6
and MuJoCo 3.8: 77 tests pass and 12 explicitly skip absent Drake/Pinocchio
SDK execution. This mixed algebra/native suite is recorded separately from
the 328-pass/25-skip native feedback platform campaign. The prescribed-motion
series, static support and stiffness checks do not establish uninterrupted
forward dynamics of a muscle-driven full body, ground/contact calibration,
private mocap agreement or all-model six-engine acceptance. Keep the existing
inventory and publication gates open.
